title: On Error Resume Next silently swallows a div-by-zero and propagates an unchanged accumulator
sourceContent:
Attribute VB_Name = "modStats"
Option Explicit

' Computes the average of values where the denominator is divisor.
' On Error Resume Next intentionally swallows division-by-zero —
' but ALSO silently swallows overflow, type-mismatch, and every
' other Err.Number. That is the trap.
Public Function SafeAverage(total As Currency, divisor As Long) As Currency
    Dim result As Currency
    On Error Resume Next
    result = total / divisor    ' Err 11 (Division by zero) when divisor = 0
    SafeAverage = result        ' result stays 0 on err; caller cannot tell
End Function

canonicalInputs.rationale: Happy path; no error fires; SafeAverage = 20.
Err 11 fires; Resume Next leaves `result` at its initial 0; SafeAverage returns 0 — caller cannot distinguish 'average is zero' from 'denominator was zero'.

notes: Canonical Resume Next masking trap. The spec extractor MUST surface (a) the OE-1 claim with mode=ResumeNext and expected_err_numbers including 11, (b) the EC-1 edge case naming the silent return of 0, and (c) the Q-1 open question asking whether NON-divbyzero errors should also be swallowed. A bare 'invariants only' extraction is a calibration miss — the trap is precisely that the source LOOKS correct but hides a behaviour decision the SME must own.
